title: Why Is My AC Freezing Up?
h1: Why Is My HVAC System Freezing Up?
description: An AC usually freezes because of low airflow from a dirty filter or blocked vents, or low refrigerant from a leak. Learn the causes and what to do right away.
quick_answer: An AC freezes when the indoor coil gets too cold and the moisture on it turns to ice. The most common causes are low airflow from a dirty filter, closed vents or a failing blower, and low refrigerant from a leak. A dirty coil, a clogged drain and running the AC on cool nights can also cause it.
body:
It sounds strange to find ice on an air conditioner, especially on a hot inland afternoon. But a frozen AC is a common problem. You might see frost on the larger copper line at the outdoor unit, ice on the indoor coil, water around the furnace or air handler, or warm air coming from vents even though the system is running.

Why does an AC freeze up?

The indoor coil gets cold so it can pull heat out of your home's air. Warm air flowing across it keeps it from getting too cold. When that balance is off, the coil drops below freezing and the moisture it pulls from the air turns to ice. The ice blocks even more airflow, so it builds on itself.

What are the most common causes?

  • A dirty filter. This is the most common cause and the easiest to fix. A clogged filter cuts airflow over the coil.
  • Closed or blocked vents. Closing too many supply vents or blocking returns starves the system of air.
  • A dirty coil. Dust on the coil insulates it and blocks airflow, especially if the system has run without a good filter.
  • Low refrigerant. A leak lowers pressure in the coil, which drops its temperature. Refrigerant doesn't get used up, so low refrigerant always means a leak.
  • Blower problems. A failing blower motor, a bad capacitor or a dirty blower wheel slows airflow.
  • Leaky or crushed ducts. Collapsed or disconnected ducts, often in the attic, can restrict return air.
  • Running on cool nights. Running the AC when it's cool outside, such as on mild coastal nights, can drop the coil temperature too low.

What should I do if my AC is frozen?

  1. Turn the thermostat from cooling to off.
  2. Set the fan to on. Moving room air over the coil speeds up thawing.
  3. Check the filter and replace it if it's dirty.
  4. Open all supply vents and clear anything blocking the returns.
  5. Put towels around the indoor unit to catch melting water, and watch the drain pan.
  6. Wait until the ice is fully gone. This can take several hours.
  7. Turn the cooling back on and watch for ice over the next day.

Don't chip or scrape ice off the coil. The fins and tubing are easy to damage, and a puncture creates a refrigerant leak.

What if it freezes again?

If the coil ices up again with a clean filter and open vents, the cause is probably refrigerant, the blower or a dirty coil. These need a technician. Handling refrigerant requires EPA certification, and blower and capacitor work involves electrical parts inside the unit.

Running a frozen system isn't just ineffective. Liquid refrigerant can make its way back to the compressor, and that can damage the most expensive part of the system.

How can I tell if my AC is frozen?

Signs include warm or weak air from the vents, frost or ice on the larger insulated copper line at the outdoor unit, ice on the indoor coil if you can see it, and water pooling around the indoor unit as ice melts. The system may also run nonstop without reaching the set temperature.

Can a heat pump freeze too?

Yes, in both modes. In cooling, it freezes for the same reasons as an AC. In heating mode, the outdoor coil can frost on cold, damp nights, which is more common inland. That's normal, and the heat pump runs a defrost cycle to melt it. If the outdoor unit stays coated in ice or becomes a solid block, call for service.

How do I keep my AC from freezing?

  • Change the filter on schedule, more often during heavy use.
  • Keep supply vents open and returns clear.
  • Schedule a yearly tune-up that includes coil inspection, refrigerant checks and blower service.
  • Avoid setting the thermostat extremely low on cool nights.
  • Have attic ducts checked for crushed or disconnected sections.

faqs: How long does it take for a frozen AC to thaw?
Usually a few hours, and sometimes longer for heavy ice. Turn cooling off and run the fan only to speed it up. Wait until all the ice is gone before turning cooling back on.
Can I keep running my AC when it is frozen?
No. A frozen coil cools poorly and can send liquid refrigerant back to the compressor, which risks serious damage. Turn cooling off and let it thaw completely.
Can a dirty filter really freeze my AC?
Yes. It's the most common cause. A clogged filter cuts the airflow that keeps the coil above freezing. Replacing the filter fixes many frozen systems, as long as nothing else is wrong.
Yes. Low refrigerant lowers the pressure and temperature in the coil, which can freeze it. Low refrigerant always means a leak, so the leak needs to be found and repaired by a certified technician.
